This vignette shows the basic workflow. The tutorial in the package repository
(`tutorial/`) covers each function in more detail.

```{r}
library(selectiveHotelling)
```

## Cluster, then test

We simulate $n = 60$ observations from three groups and cluster them with $k$-means.

```{r}
set.seed(1)
X <- rbind(matrix(rnorm(40), 20, 2),
           matrix(rnorm(40), 20, 2) + 4,
           matrix(rnorm(40), 20, 2) - 4)
res <- selective_hotelling_test(X, k1 = 1, k2 = 2, K = 3, M = 1000)
res
table(res$cluster)
```

`res$pval` is the selective p-value for the null hypothesis that the observations in
clusters 1 and 2 share one mean. The default path length is `M = 5000`; we use `M = 1000`
here so that the vignette builds quickly. The covariance matrix of the features is never
estimated.

## The naive test is not valid

When all observations come from one group, the clusters still look different, and the
classical Hotelling test rejects almost always. The selective test does not.

```{r}
set.seed(2)
X0 <- matrix(rnorm(60 * 2), 60, 2)
res0 <- selective_hotelling_test(X0, k1 = 1, k2 = 2, K = 3, M = 1000)
cl <- res0$cluster
n1 <- sum(cl == 1); n2 <- sum(cl == 2); p <- 2
F_stat <- (n1 + n2 - p - 1) / ((n1 + n2 - 2) * p) * hotelling_T2(X0, cl, 1, 2)
c(naive = pf(F_stat, p, n1 + n2 - p - 1, lower.tail = FALSE), selective = res0$pval)
```

## Other clustering algorithms

```{r}
selective_hotelling_test(X, k1 = 1, k2 = 2, K = 3, clustering = "hclust", M = 1000)$pval

cl_fun <- function(x) cutree(hclust(dist(x), method = "complete"), k = 3)
selective_hotelling_bc(X, cl_fun, k1 = 1, k2 = 2, M = 1000)$pval
```

Any function that maps a data matrix to cluster labels can be used as `cl_fun`, as long
as it gives the same labels every time it is run on the same data.
